q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: WITH CTE AS ( SELECT DISTINCT CUSTOMER_ID , COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY ) AS COUNT_P FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID ) SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CTE WHERE COUNT_P = (SELECT COUNT(*) AS C FROM PRODUCT )
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: WITH CTE AS ( SELECT DISTINCT CUSTOMER_ID , COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY ) AS COUNT_P FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID ) SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CTE WHERE COUNT_P = (SELECT COUNT(*) AS C FROM PRODUCT )
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (2, 1);
explanation: Q1 checks if the number of distinct products purchased by any customer is equal to the total number of distinct products in the database. Q2 checks if there exists at least one customer who has purchased all distinct products in the database.
counterexample_dsp: A test database with 2 products and 2 customers, where customer 1 has purchased both products, and customer 2 has purchased only product 1. Q1 will return customer 1, while Q2 will not return any customer.
